improved the outcomes and actively collaborating with State Governments 
and Industries to maximize the impact of PMKVY 4.0. The Committee hope 
that with the approval of Skill India Programme on 07.02.2025, there will be 
improvement in the physical target during the remaining part of the current 
fiscal. 
 
5. The Ministry have informed that as on 16.02.2025, the number of 
candidates enrolled, trained, assessed and certified were 31.52 lakh, 24.49 
lakh, 16.13 lakh and 14.91 lakh respectively. Thus, 78% of enrolled 
candidates were trained, 66% of trained candidates were assessed and 92% 
of assessed candidates were certified. The Committee observe that many 
candidates, who completed training were not found eligible for assessment 
due to shortage of attendance. The Committee were apprised that in order 
to streamline and improve the assessment and certification process, the 
Steering  Committee has on 12.06.2024, inter alia, approved relaxation in 
the Assessment Eligibility criteria from 70% day and 50% QP Hours AEBAS 
attendance (current provision) to overall 50% of QP Hours. Further, the 
Training Provider/Training Centre cannot start new batches in a job role 
until assessments of previous batches in the same job role are completed. 
The Committee while appreciating the measures taken by the Ministry 
expect that the decision will increase percentage of candidates assessed vis-
a-vis trained thereby resulting in consequent increase in the number of 
candidates certified and desire that efforts be made to ensure that all 
trained candidates are assessed so as to have consequential increase in the 
number of certified candidates. 
Further, it is the considered opinion of the Committee that the 
procedure adopted for assessment of Certified Candidates has to be reviewed 
and the private training providers and other agencies involved, if any, that 
do not perform to commendable extent should be blacklisted and debarred 
from being an implementing agency of the scheme. The Committee are of 

 
101 
 
the firm view that more transparent, simplified and robust assessment 
system should be put in place to look after the implementation of the 
scheme. The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in 
this regard. 
 
The Committee further  desire that  the existing infrastructure 
available with education ecosystem including Higher Education Institutes, 
ITIs, Engineering and Technical Institutes, Skill Universities, etc. need to be 
effectively utilized for running Skill India Centres (SICs).  The Committee, 
therefore, impress upon the Ministry to strengthen their monitoring and 
coordination mechanism to achieve the desired objectives. 
6.    The Committee note that as on 09.01.2025, more than 1.60 crore 
candidates have been trained under the PMKVY.  Out of them, 23.28 lakh 
candidates have been trained under PMKVY 4.0, under which placement has 
been delinked. The Committee were apprised that 24.37 lakh candidates 
were reported placed prior to implementation of PMKVY 4.0 and the reported 
placed figure has been calculated based on the certified candidates under 
STT and Special Projects of PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0 i.e. 56.88 
lakh candidates. With regard to the reasons for non-placement of the 
remaining 32.51 lakh candidates, the Ministry clarified that placements were 
tracked in STT component in the first three versions of the scheme which is 
PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0. During these phases, there were 
various challenges affecting placements, like - candidates declining job offers 
for pursuing higher studies, family obligations, wage expectations, and health 
issues; under PMKVY 3.0 Customized Crash Course Program for COVID 
Warriors and Skill Hub Initiatives did not focus on placements; COVID-19 
Pandemic created significant challenges for training providers and 
candidates, affecting the ability to secure or maintain jobs; reporting 
placement under PMKVY 1.0 was not mandatory; and difficulty in tracking 
and collection of placement documents for uploading on SIDH Portal by 
Project Implementing Agencies.  

 
102 
 
The Committee were also apprised that the certified candidates are 
tracked for one year after the certification and physical targets have been 
allocated to projects focusing on Recruit-Train-Deploy (RTD), captive 
placement, etc. In addition, placement has been prioritized in various special 
projects allocated including Industries, Industry Associations, Institutes run 
by Central Ministries/Departments/State Government agencies, etc. The 
Committee note with concern that although physical, financial and 
performance targets for PMKVY 4.0 had been fixed by the Ministry no such 
target has been stipulated for the number of placements to be made or 
number of estimated employability of the youths under the Scheme. 
Observing that although placement has been delinked under PMKVY 
4.0, the Committee are of the firm opinion that the placement statistics  is 
the real barometer for measuring the success of the Scheme and needless to 
say that the Ministry should make concerted efforts with stakeholders to 
ensure uploading of placement details of the certified candidate on Skill 
India Digital Hub (SIDH) Portal so as to have database of employment 
generated under the Scheme.  The Committee also feel that the focus of the 
Ministry should equally be concentrated on the skill enhancement of the 
candidates and generation of employment/placement for the 
trained/certified youths for which concerted efforts are warranted to achieve 
the objective of quality skill development training for enabling and 
empowering the youths to earn better livelihood.  The Committee  resolutely 
felt that the final figures of certification is the benchmark of the success and 
effectiveness of the implementation of the Scheme. Hence, the clearly 
spelling out the number of employment generated through the Scheme is 
important.   The Committee also observe that there is a critical need to 
improve the ratio between training and employment generated under the 
Scheme.  
7.   The Committee are concerned to note that under PMKVY 4.0, during the 
last three years, there is persistent shortfall in enrolment viz. 33.72 lakh in 
2022-23, 32.67 lakh in 2023-24 and 49.49 lakh in 2024-25 (upto 
09.01.2025). The physical target for 2025-26 is 30 lakh certification as 

 
103 
 
recommended by EFC in 2022 and as on 16.02.2025, only 14.91 lakh 
candidates have been certified since 2022-23. According to the Ministry, the 
staggered approvals for release of funds have impacted full-fledged roll out of 
the Scheme, leading to intermittent momentum across FY 2022-23, FY 2023-
24, and FY 2024-25. Further, in the absence of Cabinet approval, the Scheme 
was operating with staggered fund releases from the Department of 
Expenditure, leading to slow implementation and achievement of target and 
low expenditure. The Ministry have assured that since the Scheme has now 
been approved, the Ministry expect uninterrupted flow of funds, ensuring 
maximum utilization of funds and achievement of target in FY 2025-26.  
The Committee, while agreeing with the Ministry on the impact of 
enrollment due to staggered fund releases from Department of Expenditure, 
leading to slow achievement of target and appreciating the efforts made by 
the Ministry to pursue for approval of the Scheme, expect and encourage the 
Ministry to perform better in 2025-26 and honour the assurance given by 
them for optimal utilization of the funds and achievement of physical targets 
in FY 2025-26. 
 
8.  The Committee note that National Council of Applied Economic Research 
(NCAER) has been entrusted to conduct the concurrent evaluation of PMKVY 
4.0 and an agreement was signed between National Skill Development 
Corporation (NSDC) and NCAER on 20th March 2024. The Committee have 
been apprised that NCAER was supposed to submit the final report within a 
period of fourteen months, however, due to the shortage of funds, the study 
was eventually interrupted and could not be completed on time. The 
Committee have also been apprised that with the approval of the Skill India 
Programme, the Ministry are expecting uninterrupted flow of funds, and, as a 
consequence thereof, the concurrent evaluation study is likely to be 
completed by the end of 2025. The Committee trust that the exercise will be 
completed in the prescribed period. 
 

 
104 
 
9.   The Committee note that to encourage potential employers to recruit 
candidates emerging from Training Centres (TCs), the Ministry have taken 
various measures like Regular Industry Consultations,  Implementing the 
Recruit-Train-Deploy (RTD) Model, Target allocation to Industry, Priority to 
projects offering captive placements, etc. In addition, the Ministry also 
encourage Training Centres (TCs) to train under RTD model, facilitate 
placements, mobilize candidates for job melas and impart employability 
skills training. The Committee exhort the Ministry to intensify their efforts 
in supporting and hand holding the various stakeholders and other 
industries so that the placement/self-employment of the trained/certified 
candidates is enhanced to a greater extent. 
 
10.   To monitor the effectiveness of the skill training provided under 
PMKVY, the Ministry have launched SIDH. The steps taken to ensure quality 
standards across all Training Centres including PMKKs, inter alia, include 
SIDH registration, e-KYC compliance, mandatory AEBAS, virtual verification 
of operational training centres using a mobile app, feedback from candidates, 
physical visits and inspection of Training Centre, virtual monitoring through 
audio and video calls by a Kaushal Samiksha Kendra set up by MSDE.  
The Committee have been apprised that during the last three years, a 
total of 637 Physical Inspections (PIs) have been undertaken and key 
deficiencies noticed inter alia include non-conduct of training during visits, 
PMKKs closed on working days, non-compliance with equipment guidelines, 
candidates not available during visits, batch merging, low attendance (below 
50%), mismatches between physical attendance and AEBAS records, and in 
some cases, PMKKs not being found at the registered address on SIDH. The 
Ministry have informed that in order to avoid recurrence of such 
discrepancies, in addition to penal action like suspension, financial penalties 
and batch cancellation of non-compliant Centres, workshops are also 
conducted to orient PMKKs on quality delivery of training, retention of 
candidates post mobilization, maintenance of attendance etc. The 
Committee urge the Ministry to maintain the momentum for putting in place 

 
105 
 
a more invigorated monitoring mechanism so as to ensure the attainment of 
the objectives. The Committee recommend that the Ministry take proactive 
measures and impress upon the State Government, Industries and various 
stakeholders to support PMKKs wherever these have been established. 
 
11.  The Committee note that to ensure the trained candidates get 
employment as per their qualifications under PMKVY 4.0, the focus of the 
training is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career 
path and also give opportunity through various IT tools like SIDH. The 
Ministry have submitted that the job roles are aligned with the National Skill 
Qualification Committee Framework (NSQF) approved by National Skill 
Qualification Committee (NSQC) under NCVET. The Committee further note 
that identification of job roles require collaborative process that incorporates 
inputs from various stakeholders and MANDATORY On-the-Job Training (OJT) 
component in STT training to ensure practical learning and industry 
exposure. The Committee have been apprised that the scheme also focuses 
on emerging skills like Artificial Intelligence (AI), machine Learning (ML), 
AR/VR, 3D printing, and green economy sectors to cater to future industry 
needs. Considering the fact that the objective of the Scheme is to enable and 
mobilize a large number of Indian youths to take up skill training and 
become employable to sustainable livelihood, the Committee urge upon the 
Ministry to intensify the various measures put in place so as to ensure that 
maximum number of candidates get employment and sustainable livelihood 
after successful completion of the training.  
 
12.    The Committee note  that to enhance private sector involvement in 
skill development and employment under PMKVY 4.0, emphasis has been laid 
on cross utilization of infrastructure available in different institutions 
including private entities such as private educational institutions (like AICTE 
affiliated colleges, UGC approved colleges/institutes, private schools), 
Industries, Industry Associations, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs), 
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSSs), Trusts/Societies, etc. The Committee have 

 
106 
 
been apprised that target has been allocated to such reputed private sector 
institutions to impart quality skill trainings through their A&A complied 
Training Centres. The Committee desire the Ministry to take recourse to 
proactive measures and explore areas where participation of private sector in 
imparting training and providing employment to certified trained candidates 
fructify to a considerable extent. 
 
13. The Committee note that the design principles of PMKVY 4.0 provide 
for creation of a national pool of trainers and assessors to ensure their 
availability and efficient implementation of training and faster assessment 
and it has been envisaged to create a pool of 1 lakh Trainers/Assessors at 
national level. The engagement of a trainer is subject to mutual agreement 
between trainer and training provider, whereas, the assessors are aligned and 
deployed by the Assessment Agency upon receiving batch information from 
Awarding Bodies to conduct assessment of the trained candidates. The 
Committee have been apprised that 1,44,555 trainers and 75,829 assessors 
have been trained during the last three years i.e. since 2022-23,. The 
Committee appreciate that while target for creation of pool of trainers has 
exceeded the envisaged target of 1 lakh trainers, however, nearly 24,000 
Assessors are yet to be trained. The Committee call upon the Ministry to 
take urgent steps so as to ensure that the target to have 1 lakh Assessors is 
timely achieved. 
 
14.  The Committee note that as on 16.02.2025, more than 95,000 
candidates have been trained/oriented through special projects of PMKVY 
4.0, in various sectors including agriculture, handicraft and other 
traditional sectors. As per the data furnished by the Ministry, the number of 
candidates enrolled, trained, assessed and certified are 1,70,442;  95,413;  
54,226; and 50,267 respectively in 34 sectors including traditional sectors. 
While appreciating the efforts being made by the Ministry to impart sector-
specific skill training, the Committee want that emphasis be laid to provide 
training in the remaining sectors so that adequate skilled manpower is 

 
107 
 
available to cater to specific needs of the Industry. The Committee further 
want that necessary impetus be given towards implementing the policy for 
active participation of industry in framing the training programmes so as to 
effectively capture the changing requirement and realities of employment. 
The Committee also strongly feel that there has to be total 
Coordination and integration with Industry so that the skills required as per 
the demands of the Industry are identified and imparting practical training 
and experience in these trades/skill shall be given impetus. Such a measure 
can help in mitigating the skill gaps and deficiencies felt by the Industry.  
15.      The Committee note that training under PMKVY 4.0 has also been 
aligned to the requirements of new-age and futuristic job roles such as AI - 
Data Engineer, Telecom Technician - IoT Devices/Systems, Drone 
Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Additive Manufacturing (3D 
Printing), Kisan Drone Operator, Application Developer - Web & Mobile, etc. 
As on 16.02.2025, the number of candidates enrolled, trained, assessed and 
certified is 5,16,730; 3,28,501; 2,46,790 and 2,23,578 respectively. Keeping 
in view the requirements of the industry and the potential of the new age 
courses for providing employment in emerging fields, the Committee feel 
that the Ministry need to take urgent and effective steps to address the 
challenges posed and promote the courses of new-age and futuristic job 
roles. The Committee also urge the Ministry to take measures to increase 
awareness about the courses through all possible modes, including print and 
electronic media, social media, on-line advertising, outreach programmes 
etc. and further strengthen the job prospects for  trained candidates who 
pursue the new courses by working in tandem with employers to create 
adequate opportunities in the new and emerging sectors. 
 
16. The Committee have also been apprised that although  there is no 
State component under PMKVY 4.0, the Ministry are moving forward for 
increasing State engagement for implementation under PMKVY 4.0 to 
understand the district demands holistically and subsequent actions will be 
taken on the basis of responses received from Districts accordingly. The 

 
108 
 
Committee take cognizance of the Ministry’s efforts and are of the 
considered view that the steps taken by the Ministry are in right direction 
and should be persisted with so as to achieve the desired objectives. 
 
III. JAN SHIKSHAN SANSTHAN (JSS) 
 
17. The Committee appreciate that since 2021-22, 96% to 98% of physical 
targets set were achieved and during 2024-25, out of target of 5.20 lakh 
beneficiaries, 4,58,562 beneficiaries have been covered as on 19.02.2025 
and, as informed by the Ministry, with the release of second instalment of 
Grant-in-Aid following approval of the Scheme (which is one of the three 
components of Skill India Programme) by Cabinet on 07.02.2025, 5 lakh 
beneficiaries are expected to be covered by 31.03.2025 viz. 96% target will 
be achieved during 2024-25. The Committee expect the Ministry to make 
concerted efforts and honour their commitment for optimal achievement of 
the physical target for the year 2024-25.  The financial progress of the 
Scheme is, however, slow as, out of RE of Rs. 180 crore, only Rs. 72.62 
crore has been utilized up to 03.03.2025 and approximately 60% amount is 
yet to be spent. The Committee expect that with the approval of Skill India 
Programme on 07.02.2025, the Ministry will be able to utilize considerable 
amount of the unspent balance. 
 
18. The Committee note that the priority groups under JSS Scheme are 
Women, SC, ST, OBCs and minorities in rural areas and urban low-income 
areas. The Committee have been apprised that from FY 2021-22 to 26th 
January, 2025, 15,84,032 women beneficiaries; 4,74,490 Scheduled Castes 
(SCs) beneficiaries; 2,63,358 Scheduled Tribes (STs) beneficiaries; 7,27,117 
Other Backward Classes (OBCs) beneficiaries and 1,92,873 beneficiaries 
belonging to Minority Groups have been trained. The Committee, however 
note during FY 2023-24, there is decrease in training figure across all 
categories viz., Women, SC, ST, OBC, Minority and in the Financial Year 
2022-23, apart from the regular annual training target of 1800 per JSS, an 
additional target of 900 per JSSs was also provided to good performing JSSs 

 
109 
 
which led to increase in overall training figures across different categories 
(Women, SC, ST, OBC, Minority). In FY 2023-24, an Annual Training Target 
of 1800 beneficiaries per JSS was provided and no additional training target 
was provided, which shows a downfall of training figures across different 
categories (Women, SC, ST, OBC, Minority) from FY 2022-23 to FY 2023-24.  
The Committee have been apprised that in the Financial Year 2024-
25, due to migration of the JSS scheme on Skill India Digital Hub (a digital 
portal for entire skilling programme under MSDE), the training under JSS 
Scheme was initiated from June 2024 onwards. Further, in view of the 
pending Cabinet Approval for the Skill India Programme (of which JSS 
scheme is one of the three key component) which was accorded by Cabinet 
on 07.02.2025, the funds couldn’t be disbursed after release of first 
installment till the Cabinet Approval, which has also impacted the overall 
training numbers including women, SC, ST, OBC and minorities in FY 2024-
25. The Ministry have assured that the target projected for the year 2024-
25, is expected to be achieved. The Committee desire that as done during 
2022-23 additional target may be provided to good performer JSS during 
2025-26 in the larger interest of intended beneficiaries. 
19.   The Committee note that at present, 289 Jan Shikshan Sansthans are 
functional in 283 different districts across the country. Out of them, 65 
JSSs are currently functional in Aspirational Districts and 40 JSSs in LWE-
affected districts. The vision of the Ministry is to set up one JSS in each 
district of the country in a phased manner. However, at present no proposal 
for setting up of new JSSs is under consideration. Considering the fact that 
the target beneficiaries of the scheme are non-literates, neo-literates and 
persons having rudimentary level of education (70%), school dropouts up to 
class 12th (20%),and graduates (10%) in the age group of 15-45 years, the 
Committee desire that the network of JSSs be expanded to more districts 
especially in the remaining Aspirational Districts. The Committee also urge 
the Ministry to issue appropriate guidelines to the JSSs to identify the local 

 
110 
 
traditional skills/arts and provide training to candidates as per the local 
market demand. 
IV NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP PROMOTION SCHEME (NAPS-New 
Version) 
20.  The Committee note that National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme-2 
(NAPS-2) aims to promote apprenticeship training in the country by 
providing partial stipend support to the apprentices engaged under the 
Apprentice Act, 1961 and Rules made thereunder, which is limited to 25% 
of the stipend paid subject to a maximum of Rs.1500 per month per 
apprentice, which was revised six years back viz. in 2019. The Committee 
have been apprised that one of the reasons for declining apprenticeship 
engagement in the age group of 26-30 years is that the apprenticeship 
stipends which are typically lower than the regular salaries may not be 
sufficient. The Committee have also been apprised that the proposal for 
revision of minimum stipend rates is under consideration of the 
Government, which is proposed to be taken up during the 38th CAC (Central 
Apprentices Council) meeting, which is yet to be scheduled. The Committee 
desire that the matter relating to upward revision of stipend be accorded 
priority and the same be increased keeping in view the inflation and other 
relevant factors. 
21. The Committee note that NAPS – New Version has a financial outlay of 
Rs. 1942 crore for a period of four years from FY 2022-23 to FY 2025-26 
with physical target of 46 lakh apprentices over the Scheme period.  The 
Committee further note that as on 18.02.2025, the total expenditure under 
the NAPS stands at Rs. 1350.11 crore (69.52%) against the total outlay of 
Rs. 1942 crore and the physical achievement is 25.38 lakh. Thus, the 
remaining physical target stands at 20.62 lakh.   
The Committee further note that the Budget Estimates under NAPS 
for FY 2024-25 is Rs. 512.24 crore, which has been increased to Rs. 600.00 
crore at RE stage viz. there is increase of Rs. 87.76 crore, however, the 
actual expenditure as on 18.02.2025 is Rs. 381.79 crore (64% approx.) 

 
111 
 
leaving an unspent balance of Rs. 218.21 crore. The Committee have been 
apprised that the fund release under the Scheme has been restored post 
Cabinet approval for Skill India Programme on 07.02.2025 and all pending 
DBT payment will be taken care. In addition, steps for payment of stipend of 
Rs.200 crore  are being taken and, accordingly, the estimated expenditure 
will reach Rs. 582 crore by 31.03.2025. The Committee appreciate that 
despite approval of the Scheme being accorded in February, 2025, the 
Ministry will be able to incur expenditure  almost equal to enhanced RE of 
Rs. 600 crore in 2024-25.  The Committee desire that the momentum  be 
continued unabated so as to fully utilize Rs. 600 crore allocated during 
2025-26 also. 
 22. The Committee, however, find that against the physical target of 12 
lakh intended apprentices during 2024-25, as on 28.02.2025, 9 lakh 
apprentices have been engaged and 3 lakh beneficiaries are yet to be 
engaged. According to the Ministry, around one lakh apprentices are getting 
added every month. Consequently, there will still be shortfall of 2 lakh 
beneficiaries, as such, the Ministry may not be able to achieve the physical 
target set for 2024-25.  The Committee desire that the efforts be made to 
cover the remaining 20.62 lakh beneficiaries by 2025-26, being the 
culmination year of the Scheme.  
 
23.  The Committee note that as on 31st January, 2025, 21259 
establishments have engaged 8,22,196 apprentices and out of them, 6,643 
(0.81%) have been engaged by 408 establishments located in North-Eastern 
Region (NER) States. The Committee, thus find that the NER offers 
significantly lesser apprenticeship opportunities compared to the rest of the 
country. Therefore, considering the inherent issues of the States of the 
North Eastern Region, the Ministry is contemplating a Pilot project 
exclusively for NER to promote apprenticeship for which a Concept Note is 
in the draft stage. The Committee feel that implementation of the NAPS is 
marred with shortfall in North Eastern Region. The Committee would, 

 
112 
 
therefore, like to impress upon the Ministry to take up the Concept Note for 
pilot project on NER on priority basis so to undertake capacity building of 
the apprenticeship ecosystem for the people of the NER.  
24. The Committee note that while there is persistent increase in BE for 
NER during the last three years i.e. from Rs. 291.32 crore in 2022-23 to Rs. 
332.15 crore in 2023-24 to Rs. 431.31 crore (as on 15.01.2025) in 2024-25, 
the actual expenditure of the Ministry for the region has decreased during 
the corresponding period viz. from 22.83% to 22.42% to 18.26% 
respectively, i.e., more than 75% funds were not utilised every year.  The 
Committee further note that during 2024-25, as on 18.02.2025, of the total 
allocation of Rs. 431.31 crore (9.54% of Ministry’s BE) the Ministry’s NER 
expenditure is Rs. 144.12 crore and, as stated by the Ministry, it is 
estimated to reach Rs.170 crore by the end of the current fiscal, which is 
significantly higher than previous year (Rs. 74.50 crore in 2023-24 and Rs. 
66.52 crore in 2022-23). The Committee, however, find that Rs. 261.31 
crore shall still remain unutilized by 31.03.2025. Considering the fact that 
Skill India Programme has now been approved by the Cabinet, the 
Committee expect that allocation of Rs. 509.85 crore for NER will be fully 
utilized during 2025-26.  
25. The Committee, while appreciating that to promote apprenticeship, 
the Ministry have organized Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas 
(PMNAMs) at 190 locations/districts, since 2022-23 in the North Eastern 
Region (NER), wish to point out that not even a single establishment 
participated in the PMNAM organised in Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland 
and desire that while organising PMNAMs particularly in NER, it needs to be 
ensured that the registered establishments do participate in such Melas.   
 
 26. The Committee note that during 2024-25, out of 9,00,616 apprentices 
engaged as on 28.02.2025, 6,95,808 are men and 2,04,808 are women.  As 
stated by the Ministry, the difference in apprentice engagement when 
compared to FY 2023-24 has exceeded by 7,910 (4% increase than FY 2023-

 
113 
 
24) in case of women apprentices and in case of men, it is 39,596 (5.4% 
lesser than FY 2023-24). The Committee have been apprised that it is 
expected that achievement during the current FY will not be less when 
compared to FY 2023-24. The Committee have also been apprised that to 
increase women participation in apprentices, the Ministry propose to 
organize PMNAM  with a focus on mobilization from women centric 
Institutions (Women’s College and Vocational Training Centres) as well as 
development and promotion of  apprenticeship  in   Sectors with high 
growth potential and traditionally higher female participation such as 
healthcare, IT/ITES, and retail.  Observing that apprentice engagement is 
dynamic and keeps on progressing throughout the year,  the Committee 
desire that in addition to the measures being taken by the Ministry, the 
other innovative measures also need to be taken so as to increase women 
participation in apprentices so that women have access to relevant and in-
demand skills. 
27.  The Committee note that out of 25.38 lakh apprentices engaged  w.e.f. 
2022-23 upto 18.02.2025, 11.37 lakh candidates (44%) belonged to SC, ST 
and OBC [2.97 lakh SCs, 1.12 lakh STs, and 7.28 lakh OBCs].  The 
Committee have been apprised that although there is no target allocation 
based on social category, the Ministry vide letter dated 28.01.2025 have 
requested all State Commissioners/Directors dealing with Skilling/ 
Apprenticeship Training and State Skill Development Missions to further 
sensitize the identified vulnerable pockets about all  PMNAM events. The 
Committee while appreciating the steps taken by the Ministry emphasise 
that periodic review of such measures be undertaken so as to ensure that 
social category candidates are not deprived of the benefits of the Scheme. 
   
28. The Committee note that there is persistent increase in candidates 
dropped out during the last three years. During 2022-23, 2023-24, and 
2024-25, 2.34 lakh, 2.37 lakh and 2.89 lakh candidates respectively had 
dropped out from their apprentices training. The reasons for such drop out 

 
114 
 
inter-alia included  relocation challenges from place of living to 
establishment location at new location; factory/industry/establishment 
environment; cost of living; environmental conditions; health, etc.  In 
addition, attractive alternative options also lead to dropout in 
apprenticeship training.  The Committee have been apprised that the 
Ministry have taken measures like organisation of Workshops/awareness 
programmes to sensitize various stakeholders and Pradhan Mantri National 
Apprenticeship Mela (PMNAM) to facilitate as a platform to disseminate 
information on apprenticeship training.  The Ministry have also informed 
that besides revision of minimum stipend rates, efforts will also be made for 
a supportive workplace culture by establishments and States/ UTs will also 
be sensitized to make use of PMNAM/ workshops/ awareness programme to 
disseminate information for assisting interested persons to take informed 
decisions before joining the apprenticeship training. Observing that increase 
in drop out of apprentices is a matter of serious concern, the Committee 
recommend that the challenges faced by apprentices need to be addressed 
with utmost sincerity and desire that the action proposed to be taken by 
the Ministry needs to be taken to logical conclusion so as to minimize 
dropout of apprentices. 
V. NATIONAL SCHEME FOR ITIs UPGRADATION  
 
29.    Announced in budget 2024-25, the National Scheme for Upgradation of 
ITIs aims to enhance the quality and outcomes of skilling across India by 
upgrading 1,000 ITIs in a hub-and-spoke arrangement over five years. The 
BE for 2024-25 is Rs. 3000.00 crore, which has been reduced to Rs.294 
crore as the Scheme is yet to be approved by the Cabinet. For 2025-26, 
against the demand of  Rs.5010 crore, the Ministry of Finance agreed for an 
allocation of Rs.3000.00 crore. 
 
The Committee have been apprised that the Scheme has been 
recommended by the EFC in its meetings held on 09.01.2025 and 
13.01.2025, the draft Cabinet Note has received the approval of Finance 

 
115 
 
Minister on 19.02.2025 and the MSDE is in the process of obtaining 
approval of Cabinet Note. The Committee have also been apprised that since 
the approval of the Scheme is yet to be obtained, the funds could not be 
released in the FY 2024-25. The Ministry have also stated that it is expected 
that the Scheme would receive approval in the current FY and the exact 
amount of release under the scheme will depend upon the time available in 
this FY after the Cabinet approval. Meanwhile, pending the Cabinet 
approval, the Ministry have been permitted to spend only Rs. 10 crore on 
the preparatory activities of the scheme. 
  
The Committee have also been apprised that a wide range of 
stakeholder consultation involving industries, State/UT governments, and 
inter-ministerial consultation has been undertaken. In addition, Workshops 
for Technical Knowledge Exchange with four countries (China, Germany, 
Singapore, and South Korea) to arrive at the design of the scheme have also 
been conducted. The Scheme is proposed to be launched in March 2025.  
 
The Committee further note that the ITIs will be identified by State 
Governments in consultation with the industries, as per the guidelines 
issued by MSDE and the Ministry is in the process of preparing the scheme 
guidelines. The Committee have been apprised that building on the 
initiative announced in previous budget, five National Centres of Excellence 
for skilling will be set up with global expertise and partnerships to equip our 
youth with the skills required for “Make for India, Make for the World” 
manufacturing. A suitable mechanism for setting up of five National Centres 
of Excellence for skilling is under process in the Ministry, and, as informed 
by the representative of the Ministry during evidence, the Ministry propose 
to align the Scheme with National Scheme for ITI upgradation. 
 The Committee, while appreciating the efforts being made to prepare 
detailed guidelines, aligning the Scheme with the Scheme of setting up of 
five National Centres of Excellence for skilling as announced in Budget 
2025-26 and pursuing for necessary approval of the Scheme, expect that the 

 
116 
 
necessary approval will be accorded soon and the Ministry will be able to 
utilise the reduced RE during March 2025 and also budget estimates of Rs. 
3000 crore in 2025-26. 
VI. SCHEMES FOR PROMOTION OF ENTREPRENEURHIP 
 
 (i)  Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN):  
 
30. The Committee note that the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through its autonomous institutes, Indian 
Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) and National Institute of 
Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) is 
undertaking the skill development training component of PM JANMAN 
Scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) with the support of the 
Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED). It 
is aimed at targeted development of 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups (PVTGs) residing in 15 States.  
 
Under this project, a total of 500 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) are 
to be set up by TRIFED and a total of 42,000 PVTG beneficiaries are to be 
trained during 2024-25 & 2025-26. As on 19.02.2025, 174 VDVKs have been 
established and 326 VDVKs are yet to be set up. The responsibility of 
NIESBUD and IIE is to implement the skilling component of the Project 
while setting up of VDVKs lies with TRIFED. From the target of 42,000 
PVTG beneficiaries to be trained, 39,576 beneficiaries have been covered 
through Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP). Out of the total 
trained under EAP, 31,547 beneficiaries have been trained through 
Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) of which 20,492 
beneficiaries, have been further trained through Value Added Skill Training 
(VAT). The training programmes are ongoing and the Ministry have assured 
that the rest of the beneficiaries are expected to be trained before 31st 
March, 2025. The Committee expect the Ministry to make concerted efforts 
and honour their commitment to cover beneficiaries who are yet to be 

 
117 
 
trained. The Committee also desire that the remaining 326 VDVKs be set up 
by TRIFED in the larger interest of the intended beneficiaries. 
 
(ii)  PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana Entrepreneurship Skill Development 
Programme 
 
31. The Committee note that the Ministry in collaboration with the 
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) are organizing 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) on Solar Entrepreneurship 
under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. The Ministry are implementing 
the programme through their autonomous institute, NIESBUD which has 
received the sanction from the MNRE in the month of September, 2024 for 
implementing the programme during F.Y. 2024 - 25 and F.Y. 2025 – 26 with 
a total target of 50,000. 
The Committee further note that as on 28th February, 2025, the 
Institute has imparted training to 6,900 participants under the project viz., 
only14% beneficiaries have been covered and the remaining 86% are to be 
covered by 31.03.2026. The Committee impress upon the Ministry to 
intensify the efforts and cover the remaining beneficiaries by the target 
date.  
32. The Committee have been apprised that the target group to be covered 
under the programme are either the existing vendors or the new 
entrepreneurs who have the capacity to become empanelled vendors by 
submitting bank guarantee of Rs. 2.50 Lakh as per the guidelines framed by 
the MNRE. In the considered opinion of the Committee, the bank guarantee 
of Rs. 2.50 Lakh may stand a stumbling block for many especially the 
vendors in the rural areas. The Committee, therefore, desire the Ministry to 
take up the matter regarding review of the guidelines with the Ministry of 
New and Renewable Energy so as to reduce the amount of Bank guarantee.  
 
(iii)  Raising & Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP)  

 
118 
 
33. The Committee note that the Ministry through their autonomous 
Institute viz. NIESBUD are organising  Sensitization and Capacity Building 
Workshop for Women Entrepreneurs sponsored by Maharashtra Small Scale 
Industries Development Corporation Limited (MSSIDC) under Raising and 
Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) scheme of the Ministry of Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME). The Committee further note that 
the Capacity Building workshops organised by NIESBUD under the initiative 
aims to support 10,000 women-led MSMEs across Maharashtra by providing 
them with essential knowledge on key aspects such as entrepreneurial 
ecosystems, regulatory compliance, government schemes, digital marketing, 
e-commerce, financial literacy, and legal compliance for scaling their 
businesses.  
The Committee have been apprised that the project has been 
sanctioned to NIESBUD in the month of September 2024 for implementing 
the programme in F.Y. - 2024-25 and F.Y. 2025-26. During the first phase, 
NIESBUD has to impart training to 3,000 participants by 31 March, 2025 
and as on 28th  February, 2025, the Institute has imparted training to 2,207 
participants. The Committee have also been apprised that the Institute has 
mobilised the participants for the remaining target and is organising the 
programmes in different districts of Maharashtra, as such, the allocated 
target will be completed by 31st March 2025. The Ministry have also stated 
that in the second phase, the Institute is required to train 7,000 
participants by 31st March 2026. 
The Committee find that while 30% target will be achieved by 
31.03.2025, the remaining 70% beneficiaries will be required to be covered 
in 2025-26. The Committee, therefore, call upon the Ministry to draw a road 
map for achieving the target within the stipulated time.   
(iv) Capacity Building for Fair Price Shop Owners (FPS) 
34. The Committee note that the Ministry in collaboration with the 
Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Ministry of Consumer 

 
119 
 
Affairs, Food and Public Distribution have undertaken a Capacity Building 
Programme for Fair Price Shop (FPS) Owners. The project is aimed to enable 
the FPS owners to run their businesses in consonance with the 
contemporary practices being adopted by Retail Entrepreneurs. The 
Committee have been apprised that the Ministry, through their autonomous 
Institute viz. NIESBUD is responsible for training and capacity building, 
while the nomination of participants is provided by DFPD in consultation 
with the respective State Food Distribution Departments. The total target 
under the project is to train 3000 FPS owners by 31st March, 2026 and, out 
of them, the number of beneficiaries trained till 20th February, 2025 is 318 
and further training of 300 more beneficiaries is planned to be completed by 
31.03.2025. 
The Committee, thus, find that while 20% target will be achieved by 
31.03.2025, the remaining 80% beneficiaries will be required to be covered 
in 2025-26. The Committee call upon the Ministry to coordinate with DFPD 
and achieve the target as stipulated above. 
VII. PROJECT 'SWAVALAMBINI WOMEN ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
PROGRAMME' 
 
35. The Committee note that the Project 'Swavalambini Women 
Entrepreneurship Programme' is specifically targeted at female students of 
colleges and universities. NIESBUD, Noida and the IIE, Guwahati, will be the 
Implementing Agency (IA) of the Project 'Swavalambini' of MSDE in 
collaboration with NITI Aayog.   The initiative will focus on empowering 
female students in Higher Education Institutions (HEIS) by providing them 
with essential skills, mentorship, and access to resources necessary for 
starting and scaling successful businesses. The Project will focus on 
comprehensive entrepreneurship training/ capacity-building combining 
theory-based training with practical exposure through experiential learning.   
 
The Committee further note that the Project will be implemented  in 
Banaras Hindu University and Chaudhary Charan Singh University (North 

 
120 
 
Zone-Uttar Pradesh);  University of Hyderabad, Maulana Azad National Urdu 
University, (South Zone-Telangana);  Kiang Nangba Government College, 
Jowai, Ri- Bhoi College, Ri Bhoi and North Eastern Hill University (NEHU), 
Shillong (North East Zone-Meghalaya);  Government Champai College, 
Lunglei Government College and Mizoram University (North East Zone-
Mizoram); and Gauhati University, Handique College and Dispur College 
(North East Zone-Assam). The target of the Project is to train 1200 female 
students under Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme (NIESBUD - 600, IIE 
- 600), out of which, 600 will be further selected for the Women 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (NIESBUD-300, IIE - 300).  
 
The Committee were apprised that the Ministry of Skill Development 
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in collaboration with NITI Aayog and Women 
Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) as knowledge partner, have recently 
launched the Swavalambini Women Entrepreneurship Programme on 07th 
February, 2025 in North Eastern States of India viz. Meghalaya, Mizoram 
and Assam.  The Committee impress upon the Ministry to take necessary 
steps to ensure that the Project is launched/implemented in the already 
selected Higher Education Institutions (HEIS) of the remaining two States 
viz. Uttar Pradesh and Telengana. 
 
36. The Committee have been apprised that the programme will be 
implemented in four phases and will include Faculty Development 
Programmes (FDP) of 5 days for selected faculty members from colleges, 
Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP) of 2 days for 1,200 students, 
Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) of 40 hours for selected 
600 students, followed by 6 months of mentoring and handholding support 
to ensure sustained guidance and business development assistance. The 
Committee desire that it would be in the fitness of things if  the feedback is 
also obtained from trained faculty and students selected as well as trained 
after every phase of the Project so as to have an objective assessment of 
shortcomings as well as improvement in future training programmes. 
 

 
121 
 
37. The Committee have also been apprised that over the past ten years, 
both NIESBUD and IIE have collectively trained 12,33,699 candidates 
through various programs and interventions, demonstrating their 
significant contribution to the entrepreneurial ecosystem and notably, 
7,06,617 (57.27%) of these trainees have been women. The Committee 
appreciate the contribution made by both NIESBUD and IIE and their 
commitment to promoting women’s entrepreneurship and inclusive 
economic growth and desire both organizations  to maintain momentum so 
as to ensure attainment of the  objectives of the  Project. 
VIII  PM-VISHWAKARMA  
38. The Committee note that PM Vishwakarma Scheme was launched on 
17th September, 2023, which aims at upskilling the Vishwakarma’s with the 
knowledge of modern tools and techniques coupled with credit support for 
expanding their business. The Scheme is being implemented by three 
Ministries i.e., Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), and 
Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance and MSDE is 
the nodal ministry for implementation of Skilling Component of the 
Scheme. A total of 18 trades are covered under the Scheme to promote 
onboarding of training centres under the scheme.  
    The Committee note that as on 15.02.2025, PMV id is available in 679 
districts, however, training has been initiated in 636 districts, the training 
is yet to be initiated in 43 districts. Further, 26,96,358 PMV ID are available 
and as on 15.02.2025, 18,99,385 candidates have been trained and assessed 
against the target of 16 lakh candidates for 2023-24 and 2024-25.  
The Committee observe that the PM Vishwakarma Yojana is currently 
available in 34 out of 36 States/ Union Territories except Tamil Nadu and 
West Bengal. The Ministry have stated that the State Monitoring Committee 
and District Implementation Committees have not yet been constituted by 
these two States. The Committee recommend the Ministry to take up the 

 
122 
 
matter with the two State Governments without any further delay and 
resolve the issue so that products and services of artisans of the two States 
also have their benevolent share in domestic and global value chains. The 
Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard. 
39. The Ministry have further stated that the concerned State 
Governments and Regional Directorates of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship will work together to identify suitable training centers to 
initiate training in the remaining 43 districts. The Committee desire the 
Ministry to strengthen their coordination and monitoring mechanism so as 
to ensure identification and operationalisation of Training Centres in 43 
disticts on urgent basis so that the deserving artisans peddle their products 
and services into domestic and global value chains.  
IX. SKILL ACQUISITION AND KNOWLEDGE AWARENESS FOR LIVELIHOOD 
PROMOTION (SANKALP) 
40. The Committee note that the Skill Acquisition and Knowledge 
Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP) was conceived to support 
National Skill Development Mission (NSDM) in achieving its full potential.  
The Scheme was conceptualized to operationalize Skill India Mission by 
setting in motion the sub-Missions proposed under the NSDM. It is a US $ 
250 million (Rs.1,650 crore) World Bank Loan assisted Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of the MSDE. The Scheme was made effective on 19th January, 
2018 with an initial implementation period till March, 2023, which has been 
extended till March, 2025.  The Committee further note that the World 
Bank has reviewed the project deliverables during Implementation 
Completion Mission (ICM) in March 2024 and submitted an Implementation 
Status and Results Report, in which they have rated the project's 
performance as 'Satisfactory’.  
The Committee have been apprised that the targets set for all the four 
Project Development Objectives (PDOs) under the Scheme have been 
achieved.  The Committee have also been apprised that the targets for all 
the Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) have been achieved except for 

 
123 
 
DLI7, which is under verification by the Independent Verification Agency 
and is expected to be completed by March 2025. The Committee exhort the 
Ministry to make sincere efforts and ensure that verification of the 
remaining Disbursement Linked Indicator viz. DL17 is completed by 31st 
March, 2025.  Further, as informed by the Ministry, at present, there is no 
proposal to extend the Scheme beyond March, 2025 or introduce any other 
Scheme on similar lines. The Committee, therefore, recommend that an 
impact assessment of the Scheme be undertaken during 2025-26 and 
completed in a time bound manner. 
X. MISCELLANEOUS 
(i) Skill Development and upliftment of Tea Plantation Workers 
41. The Committee note that Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and 
Karnataka are the major tea growing States. However, there is no job role 
exclusively related to Tea Plantation Workers under PMKVY 4.0. 
Considering the fact that tea plantations contribute significantly to 
employment and overall economic growth, the Committee recommend the 
Ministry to explore job role related skill training for Tea Plantation Workers 
under PMKVY 4.0 and set up JSSs in the remaining districts of these States 
so as to improve the income generation and livelihood of Tea Plantation 
Workers of the country.  
(ii) Review of National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 
42.   The Committee note that the ‘Review of National Policy for Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship’ Project was assigned to BCG India, 
which has submitted the draft National Policy Document in December 2024 
and the same is being reviewed in consultation with key stakeholders. The 
Committee call upon the Ministry to strengthen their coordination 
mechanism, analyse the views/suggestions of key stakeholders and 
complete the review exercise in a time bound manner so as to inter alia 

 
124 
 
enhance skill development ecosystem and foster lifelong learning to 
improve employability and meet the evolving needs of the economy. 
 
(iii) Setting up of 30 Skill India International Centres (SIICs) 
 
43. The Committee were apprised during evidence on 19.11.2024, that it is 
proposed to set up 30 Skill India International Centres (SIICs) to promote 
skill based International mobility. The Committee have now been apprised 
that while two SIICs have been established at Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) and 
Bhubaneswar (Odisha), the work relating to setting up of additional 5 SIICs at 
Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship, Guwahati (Assam); NSTI, Bengaluru 
(Karnataka); NSTI, Ludhiana (Punjab); NSTI, Hyderabad (Telangana) and NSTI, 
Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), is in advanced stage. The Committee desire that 
appropriate steps be taken on priority to ensure that the remaining Skill 
India International Centres are set up and made operational in a time bound 
manner so as to facilitate international workforce mobility opportunities for 
Indians and achieve the objective of making India the skill capital of the 
world. The Committee would like to be apprised of progress made in this 
regard.  
 
(iii) Action taken on the Observations/Recommendations of the 
Committee contained in their Third Report (18 LS) on Demands for 
Grants (2024-25) 
 
44. The Committee trust that the Ministry have taken appropriate action 
on the Observations/Recommendations of the Committee contained in their 

 
125 
 
Third Report on Demands for Grants (2024-25) of the Ministry, which was 
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 16.12.2024.

I. COVERAGE OF THE ESI SCHEME 
 
(Recommendation Para No. 1) 
 
5. The Committee, in their Fifty-First Report, had noted that the ESI Act, 1948 
applies to factories employing 10 or more persons. The Central Government is fully 
responsible for running the Scheme and ESIC does not receive subsidy from the 
Government.  Presently, the employees of factories and establishments covered 
under the Act drawing wages up to Rs.21,000 per month (Rs.25,000 for Persons 
with Disabilities) are covered under the Scheme. The Employees’ and Employers’ 
contribution was reduced from 1.75% to 0.75% and 4.75% to 3.25% of the wages 
w.e.f. 01.07.2019. There was overall reduction in contribution from 6.5%to 4% 
(2.5% decrease). The proceeds are utilized to provide medical care and various cash 
benefits to the Insured Persons (IPs). The average daily wages during a wage period 
for exemption from payment of employee’s contribution which was Rs.137 earlier 
was raised to Rs.176 w.e.f. 06 September 2019. 
 
6. The Committee had further noted that the number of IPs in 2018-19, 2019- 
20, 2020-21 and 2021-22 was 3.50, 3.41, 3.39 and 3.10 crore respectively, and 
the number of beneficiaries during the corresponding period was 13.56, 13.24, 
13.16 and 12.04 crore.  Thus, there is noticeable decrease in IPs as well as 
beneficiaries since 2018-19. The reasons for decrease in the number of IPs as well 
as beneficiaries, as intimated by the Ministry, include, inter-alia out-break of the 
Covid-19 Pandemic owing to which the companies/ factories were completely shut 
down and employees working in such companies were compelled to leave the place 
of work for some period. 
 
7. The Committee had also noted that the net revenue for two years prior to 
reduction of the contribution was Rs.43,274 crore and for three years following the 

3 
 
reduction, it was Rs.44,587 crore. Thus, the average annual revenue prior to, and 
after the reduction of the contribution is Rs.21,637 crore and Rs.14,862 crore 
respectively. Thus, the average annual reduction of ESIC’s revenue following the 
cutting down of the contribution was to the extent of Rs.6775 crore. 
 
8. As intimated by the Ministry, presently, there is no proposal to change the 
wage limit for coverage under the ESI Scheme. 
 
9. The Committee had wished to highlight the fact that with the passage of time, 
wages have increased. The last revision of the wage ceiling was affected from 01 
January 2017 viz. approx. 6 years 9 months back and the prevailing wage limit of 
Rs.176 per day for exemption from paying contribution was effected w.e.f. 06 
September 2019. In the light of the changing economic scenario, the Committee 
had impressed upon the Ministry/ESIC the need for reviewing the provisions 
relating to coverage, contribution and entitlement of wages.  An expert Committee 
could be constituted for suggesting the changes ‘required’ in the provisions with a 
view to increasing coverage by a considerable extent and provide benefits to 
maximum number of IPs and beneficiaries. The Committee had wished to be 
apprised of the action taken in this regard. 
  
10. In their Action Taken Note furnished to the Committee, the Ministry of 
Labour & Employment have stated as follows:- 
 
 “The decision regarding upward revision of wage ceiling for ESI coverage 
 and other issues are taken after comprehensive exercise to assess as to 
 whether the existing ESI infrastructure would be able to meet the 
 requirement of the employees and families, which are likely to increase 
 consequent upon of the enhanced wage ceiling.  At present, there are 165 
 ESI hospitals, 1695 ESI dispensaries and 869 Insurance Medical 
 Practitioners (IMPs) across the country.     
 
 For the purpose, a committee comprising the officers and members of the 
 ESI Corporation had been constituted for examination of the issue and 
 make suitable recommendations.  The report of the committee has been 
 received recently and issue is under examination”. 
 
11. Impressing upon the Ministry/ESIC the need for reviewing the 
provisions relating to coverage, contribution and entitlement of wages under 
the Employees State insurance (ESI) Scheme, the Committee had desired that 

4 
 
an expert committee be constituted for suggesting the changes ‘required’ in 
the provisions. In their Action Taken Note furnished to the Committee, the 
Ministry have intimated that a committee comprising of officers and 
members of the ESI Corporation had been constituted for the purpose. 
Further, the report of the committee has since been received and the issue 
is under examination. However, there is no specific decision taken by the 
Ministry/ESIC. Given the increase in wages over the passage of time and the 
fact that the last revision of wage ceiling was effected in 2017 while the wage 
limit for exemption from paying contribution was last revised in 2019, the 
Committee stress the urgency for an upward revision of wage ceiling and 
exemption limit under the ESI Scheme and urge the Ministry/ESIC to 
examine the report in all urgency and in the least possible time so that the 
wage ceiling and exemption limit are enhanced accordingly with a view to 
substantially increase coverage and provide benefits to maximum number of 
IPs and beneficiaries. The action taken in this regard may be communicated 
to this Committee immediately. 
 
II. EXTENDED COVERAGE UNDER CODE ON SOCIAL SECURITY, 2020 
  
(Recommendation Para No. 2) 
 
12. The Committee had noted that the ESI Act, 1948 along with 8 other Central 
Labour Acts has been subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020 (Act 36 of 
2020) which was notified on 29 September, 2020. The code is, however, yet to be 
enforced. The Central Government has notified the Code on Social Security 
(Central) Rules, 2020 in the Gazette of India on 13 November 2020 for stakeholder 
consultation; and the final rules are yet to be notified. 
 
13. The benefits currently available under the ESI Act will be retained in the 
Code. All the benefits relating to medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and 
dependence benefits are proposed to be retained.  The coverage of ESI will expand 

5 
 
pan India to all establishments employing ten or more employees under the Code 
as against only the notified district areas currently. 
 
14. The Committee had further noted that as per Section 1(4) of the Code on 
Social Security, 2020 read with its First Schedule, provision has been made for 
voluntary coverage of establishments with less than 10 persons.  At present, the 
ESI Act does not contain this provision.  Coverage of plantations as an 
establishment, on opting for the same by the employer has been provided for in the 
Code. As per the proviso of First Schedule of the Code, ibid, establishments 
engaged in hazardous or life-threatening occupations will have to cover every single 
employee. Provision for formulating special scheme for unorganized workers, gig 
workers, platform workers and other beneficiaries have been included in the Code. 
As per the provisions of Section 142 of the Code on Social Security, 2020, the 
establishment of identity through Aadhaar for the employees or unorganized 
workers or any other person, either for himself or dependents, has been made 
mandatory for availing services, seeking benefits, receiving payment, etc. Further, 
the definition of ‘wages’ under ESI Act, 1948 is proposed to be replaced with the 
definition of ‘wages’ as contained under Code on Social Security 2020.  The Code 
defines ‘wages’ under Section 2(88) as basic pay plus dearness allowance plus 
retaining allowance.  The definition excludes bonus, conveyance allowance, 
PF/pension contribution, payment towards special expenses because of the nature 
of the job, HRA, remuneration payable under settlement between parties or the 
order of the Tribunal, overtime allowance, commission, etc. The proviso to the 
section in the Code states that if the total of the components that are excluded is 
more than 50% of gross remuneration, then such percentage of remuneration, 
which is in excess of 50% will be added to the wages. 
 
15. The Committee had noted that with the implementation of the Code, the 
coverage of ESI is to expand pan-India. The Ministry have admitted that 
considering the existing infrastructure, expanding the coverage without proper 
development/ augmentation of facilities will not be in the interest of Insured 
Persons/beneficiaries.  The Committee were also concerned to note that out of 3.73 
crore Insured Persons (IPs) as on 12 May 2023, Aadhaar numbers of only 17,531 
IPs have been seeded by ESIC. 
 
16. The Committee had expressed concern to note that at present the 
Ministry/ESIC is not fully geared up to provide extended coverage as envisaged 
under the Code on Social Security, 2020. The Committee were of the considered 
view that preparatory work for implementation of the plan of action already 
identified by ESIC, viz conduct of extensive surveys; collection of data from 
Government Departments; identification of common  business identifiers for 
establishments by the ESIC in consultation with EPFO; use of Aadhar for 

6 
 
identification of members/insured persons, etc. need to be undertaken in right 
earnest. The Committee had also urged upon the Ministry to seriously have a re-
look at its approach for gearing up the medical/health infrastructure, prepare a 
‘Vision Document’ and ensure that administrative, infrastructural, legal, technical 
and financial hurdles do not in any way dilute the spirit of Code on Social 
Security, 2020 for pan India coverage  of  ESI  Scheme  in  the larger   interest  of 
present  and  future beneficiaries including those in the Unorganized Sectors, as 
also gig workers,  platform workers and similar other beneficiaries. 
  
17. In their Action Taken Note furnished to the Committee, the Ministry of 
Labour & Employment have stated as follows:- 
 
“In order to identify the uncovered factories/establishments/employees 
 under the ESI scheme, field offices are  advised to liaise with EPFO, other 
departments of the state and central government, local offices like  Central   
Board of Secondary Education, universities, Food and Drugs 
 Administration, field offices of Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of 
 Industries, Ministry of Corporate affairs, MSME, GST,  Confederation of 
 Indian Industry, etc. and obtain data available with them regarding 
 factories/establishment registered with them. 
 
 The data as collected is scrutinized at the level of the field offices of the 
 ESIC (regional and sub-regional offices) across the country and to units, 
 which are found to be coverable under ESI scheme, letters are issued to 
 them explaining the benefits under the scheme and requesting for 
 coverage under it.  
 
 The field offices were again communicated on 21.09.2023 for liaisoning 
 with EPFO and other departments/ offices for obtaining data available 
 with them regarding factories/establishment registered thereon.  As per 
 the data received, there were a total of 291283 factories/ establishments 
 identified for coverage under the ESI scheme and 92089 were non-
 coverable. 
  
At present, the ESI scheme has been notiﬁed in 674 districts out of 778 
 districts of the country, which includes 571 fully notiﬁed districts under 
 ESI coverage and 103 partially notiﬁed districts under ESI coverage. 
 There are remains 104 districts where the ESI scheme is yet to be  notiﬁed. 
Thus, there is a total of 207 districts (103 partially notiﬁed  districts and 
104 non-notified districts) which are awaiting full coverage  under ESI 
scheme.

18. The Committee acknowledge the measures taken by the Ministry/ESIC 
towards extending the coverage of the ESI Scheme as envisaged under the 
Code on Social Security 2020.  However, as far as implementation of the ESI 
Scheme in non-notified areas/districts, recruitment process of existing

the Rules should be notified immediately. The Committee, also desire that 
the Ministry in co-ordination with ESIC undertake a phased and strategic

of the firm opinion that these steps will ensure the evolution of ESIC into a

guaranteed success in preparing the groundwork before the Social Security

CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS 
WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
  
(Recommendation Para No. 1) 
  
 
The ESI Act, 1948 applies to factories employing 10 or more persons. The 
Central Government is fully responsible for running the Scheme and ESIC does 
not receive subsidy from the Government. Presently, the employees of factories and 
establishments covered under the Act drawing wages up to Rs.21,000 per month 
(Rs.25,000for Persons with Disabilities) are covered under the Scheme. The 
Employees’ and Employers’ contribution was reduced from 1.75% to 0.75% and 
4.75% to 3.25% of the wages w.e.f. 01.07.2019. There was overall reduction in 
contribution from 6.5% to 4% (2.5% decrease). The proceeds are utilized to provide 
medical care and various cash benefits to the Insured Persons (IPs). The average 
daily wages during a wage period for exemption from payment of employee’s 
contribution which was Rs.137 earlier was raised to Rs.176 w.e.f. 06 September 
2019. 
 
The Committee further note that the number of IPs in 2018-19, 2019- 20, 
2020-21 and 2021-22 was 3.50, 3.41, 3.39 and 3.10 crore respectively, and the 
number of beneficiaries during the corresponding period was 13.56, 13.24, 13.16 
and 12.04 crore.  Thus, there is noticeable decrease in IPs as well as beneficiaries 
since 2018-19. The reasons for decrease in the number of IPs as well as 
beneficiaries, as intimated by the Ministry, include, inter alia out-break of the 
Covid-19 Pandemic owing to which the companies/ factories were completely shut 
down and employees working in such companies were compelled to leave the place 
of work for some period. 
 
The Committee also note that the net revenue for two years prior to reduction 
of the contribution was Rs.43,274 crore and for three years following the reduction, 
it was Rs.44,587 crore. Thus, the average annual revenue prior to, and after the 
reduction of the contribution is Rs.21,637 crore and Rs.14,862 crore respectively. 
Thus, the average annual reduction of ESIC’s revenue following the cutting down 
of the contribution was to the extent of Rs.6775 crore. 
 
As intimated by the Ministry, presently, there is no proposal to change the 
wage limit for coverage under the ESI Scheme. 
 

27 
 
The Committee wish to highlight the fact that with the passage of time, wages 
have increased. The last revision of the wage ceiling was affected from 01 January 
2017 viz. approx. 6 years 9 months back and the prevailing wage limit of Rs.176 
per day for exemption from paying contribution was effected w.e.f. 06 September 
2019. In the light of the changing economic scenario, 
the   Committee   impress   upon   the   Ministry/ESIC   the   need   for 
reviewing the provisions relating to coverage, contribution and entitlement of 
wages.  An expert Committee could be constituted for suggesting the changes 
‘required’ in the provisions with a view to increasing coverage by a considerable 
extent and provide benefits to maximum number of IPs and beneficiaries. The 
Committee wish to be apprised of the action taken in this regard.

For the purpose, a committee comprising the officers and members of the 
ESI Corporation had been constituted for examination of the issue and make

11021/14/2020-SS-I dated 18.06.2024] 
  
  
Comments of the Committee 
Please see Para No. 11 of Chapter-I 
  
(Recommendation Para No. 2) 
 
The ESI Act, 1948 along with 8 other Central Labour Acts has been 
subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020 (Act 36 of 2020) which was notified 
on 29September, 2020.The code is, however, yet to be enforced. The Central 
Government has notified the Code on Social Security (Central) Rules, 2020 in the 
Gazette of India on 13 November 2020 for stakeholder consultation; and the final 
rules are yet to be notified. 
 

28 
 
The benefits currently available under the ESI Act will be retained in the 
Code. All the benefits relating to medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and 
dependence benefits are proposed to be retained.  The coverage of ESI will expand 
pan India to all establishments employing ten or more employees under the Code 
as against only the notified district areas currently. 
 
The Committee further note that as per Section 1(4) of the Code on Social 
Security, 2020 read with its First Schedule, provision has been made for voluntary 
coverage of establishments with less than 10 persons.  At present, the ESI Act does 
not contain this provision.  Coverage of plantations as an establishment, on opting 
for the same by the employer has been provided for in the Code. As per the proviso 
of First Schedule of the Code, ibid, establishments engaged in hazardous or life-
threatening occupations will have to cover every single employee. Provision for 
formulating special scheme for unorganized workers, gig workers, platform workers 
and other beneficiaries have been included in the Code. As per the provisions of 
Section 142 of the Code on Social Security, 2020, the establishment of identity 
through Aadhaar for the employees or unorganized workers or any other person, 
either for himself or dependents, has been made mandatory for availing services, 
seeking benefits, receiving payment, etc. Further, the definition of ‘wages’ under 
ESI Act, 1948 is proposed to be replaced with the definition of ‘wages’ as contained 
under Code on Social Security 2020.  The Code defines ‘wages’ under Section 2(88) 
as basic pay plus dearness allowance plus retaining allowance.  The definition 
excludes bonus, conveyance allowance, PF/pension contribution, payment 
towards special expenses because of the nature of the job, HRA, remuneration 
payable under settlement between parties or the order of the Tribunal, overtime 
allowance, commission, etc. The proviso to the section in the Code states that if 
the total of the components that are excluded is more than 50% of gross 
remuneration, then such percentage of remuneration, which is in excess of 50% 
will be added to the wages. 
 
The Committee note that with the implementation of the Code, the coverage 
of ESI is to expand pan-India. The Ministry have admitted that considering the 
existing infrastructure expanding the coverage without proper development/ 
augmentation of facilities will not be in the interest of Insured 
Persons/beneficiaries.  The Committee are also concerned to note that out of 3.73 
crore Insured Persons (IPs) as on 12 May 2023, Aadhaar numbers of only 17,531 
IPs have been seeded by ESIC. 
 
The Committee express concern to note that at present the Ministry/ESIC is 
not fully geared up to provide extended coverage as envisaged under the Code on 
Social Security, 2020. The Committee are of the considered view that preparatory 

29 
 
work for implementation of the plan of action already identified by ESIC viz. 
conduct of extensive surveys; collection of data from Government Departments; 
identification of common   business identifiers for establishments by the ESIC in 
consultation with EPFO; use of Aadhar for identification of members/insured 
persons, etc. need to be undertaken in right earnest. The Committee also urge 
upon the Ministry to seriously have  a re-
look  at  its  approach  for  gearing  up  the medical/health infrastructure, 
prepare a ‘Vision Document’ and ensure that administrative, infrastructural, legal, 
technical and financial hurdles do notin any way dilute the spirit 
of  Code  on  Social Security,  2020  for  pan  India 
coverage   of   ESI   Scheme   in   the   larger   interest   of present  and  future 
beneficiaries including those in the Unorganized Sectors, as also gig 
workers,  platform workers and similar other beneficiaries. 
  
(Reply of Government) 
 
In order to identify the uncovered factories/establishments/employees 
under the ESI scheme, field offices are  advised to liaise with EPFO, other 
departments of the state and central government, local offices like Central Board 
of Secondary Education, universities, Food and Drugs Administration, filed offices 
of Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Industries, Ministry of Corporate affairs, 
MSME, GST,  Confederation of Indian Industry, etc. and obtain data available with 
them regarding factories/establishment registered with them. 
 
The data as collected is scrutinized at the level of the field offices of the ESIC 
(regional and sub-regional offices) across the country and to units, which are found

obligation to ensure that their share of contribution is paid to ESIC within six-
monthly intervals in a financial year.  In case of default by the employer in payment 
of contribution, recovery is affected after following the procedure laid down. If the 
employer is not contributing deliberately and if the stipulated time period is 
exceeded, there is no provision for the employee to voluntarily contribute his 
share.  The Committee note that despite penal provisions being available under 
ESI Act, Negotiable Instruments Act and various Sections of IPC for taking action 
against wilfull defaulter employers, there are occasions where the employee, 
despite having contributed his share, is made to suffer on account of default on 
the part of the employer. 
  
The Committee express concern in this regard and desire that the Ministry 
strengthen the monitoring mechanism, ensure strict enforcement of the penal 
provisions so as to deter violators and also devise a suitable mechanism to prevent 
such instances, which would minimize the sufferings of the employees.

The Committee note that the norms for setting up of ESI Hospitals in the 
country depend upon the minimum number of IPs in the catchment area ranging 
from minimum of 50,000 to 5,00,000 IPs. For 100 bedded hospitals, the catchment 
area should have at least 50,000 IPs, and for 600 bedded hospitals, the catchment 
area should have at least 5,00,000 IPs.  The Committee further note that the IP 
population is taken in a radius of 25 Km and there should not be any other ESI 
Hospital within a radius of 50 Km. Further, if there is another ESI Hospital existing 
within 50 Km, then each ESI Hospital should fulfill these norms in the respective 
catchment area viz., if the two hospitals are at a distance of 40 Km, then each 
hospital should meet these norms within the 20 Km radius. The Committee have 
also been apprised that the norms have since been updated in June 2022, which, 
inter alia provide that instead of considering the present IP population, health 
facilities may be created based on projected number of IP population in future viz., 
upcoming 05 years in case of hospitals, and 03 years in case of dispensaries. 
 
In case of non-notified districts or non-notified areas of partially 
implemented districts, new dispensaries may be established based on number of 
coverable employees instead of Insured Persons, as ascertained in the pre-
implementation survey data.

ESI Corporation during its 188th meeting held on 18/19th June 2022 has

futuristic number of IP Population in upcoming 05 years in case of hospitals and 
03 years in case of dispensaries.

The Committee note that with a view to providing facilities for early detection 
and diagnosis of Occupational Diseases among ESI beneficiaries, ESIC has at 
present established Occupational Disease Centres (ODCs) in only 07 States/UTs. 
While 02 ODCs are located in ESIC hospitals at Basaidarapur (New Delhi) and 
Indore (Madhya Pradesh), the other five ODCs are located in medical colleges at 
Faridabad (Haryana), Joka (Kolkata), Alwar (Rajasthan), Bihta (Patna) and K. K. 
Nagar (Chennai). These ODCs also cater to the needs of ESI beneficiaries of the 
neighbouring States, which refer the suspected cases. The Committee have also 
been apprised that State run ESIS hospitals are being identified to develop ODCs 
in States where ESIC hospitals are not available. The Committee further note that 
an MoU with ICMR-National Institute of Occupational Health, Ahmedabad has 
been signed to undertake research. 
  
The Committee find that there are inherent provisions in the ESI Act, 1948, 
which recognize occupational disease as an employment injury and insured 
persons become eligible for permanent disability benefit on the basis of 
identification of occupational disease. Considering the provisions contained in the 
Act, it is imperative on the part of the Ministry/ESIC to pay special and focused 
attention on early detection and diagnosis of occupational diseases. This can be 
achieved in the real sense by increasing the ODCs in various parts of the country, 
especially where the number of cases reported are on the higher side. 
  
The Committee also desire that the process of identification of ESIS hospitals 
for the purpose of development of ODCs be expedited. Further, as no laboratory 
has been established in ESIC or ESIS Hospitals for the purpose of research, the 
Committee recommend the Ministry/ESIC to consider setting up their own 
laboratories for undertaking research activities so as to minimize the dependence 
on other sources for medical services. 
  
(Reply of Government)

surveillance and timely diagnosis of occupational diseases in the IP population for 
promoting workplace safety and ensuring the welfare of workers across industries.

the month of April 2023 which is examining the work-related illness data on 
regular basis.Based on the outcome of work-related illness profiling and outcomes,

The Committee have, time and again, expressed concern on the existence of 
large number of vacancies in the ESIC/ESIS hospitals and dispensaries, which 
adversely impacts the health services. The steps taken by the Ministry/ESIC to fill 
up the vacancies have not yielded the desired results and the situation continues 
to be bleak at the ground level. On in- depth analysis of the data furnished by the

doctors, 26 % of posts of nurses and 53% posts of para-medical staff were vacant

vacant as on March 2023. In the case of 36 dispensaries run by ESIC, 43% posts

in July, 2023. (Jharkhand 72%, Bihar 64%, Goa 57% & Odisha 52%). It is equally 
a matter of concern that 45% of the posts in various cadres of the ESIC remained 
vacant as on July 2023. 
  
The Ministry/ESIC have attempted to rationalize their position by indicating 
the progress of recruitment exercise undertaken/under process / proposed to be 
undertaken to fill up the vacancies at various levels. The Committee are, however, 
not convinced with the response of the Ministry/ESIC. Very glaringly, in some 
cases, make shift arrangements have been made through contractual engagements 
against regular vacancies. 
  
The Committee trust that the orders of DoPT, Government of India with 
regard to the time period for which the sanctioned posts in various cadres could 
be   kept vacant are being complied with by the Ministry.
