Special Campaign on Swachta and reducing pendency in Government offices: 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.47 The Committee applauds the Department in bringing out such innovative ideas  for 
cleanliness campaign. The Committee hopes that the Department will hold such  campaigns 
every year. The Committee expects the Department to widen  the scope of such campaigns so 
that more number of offices can be included in the campaign. (3.25) 
Action Taken  
1.48 From 2021, the Government of India has started a month -long Special Campaign 
from 2nd -31st October every year on the Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) and 
institutionalizing Swachhata at work place in all Central Ministries/Departments including 
their attached/subordinate offices.  Two Special Campaigns have been conducted so far in the 
year 2021 and 2022. 
1.49 The Special campaign in the year 2021, organized from 2nd —31st October, 2021 
focussed on Ministries/ Departments and had very encouraging outcome s. Swachhata 
camapigns were made at 5,968 sites.  About 12 lakh square feet of space was freed from 
scrap and outlived records and Rs 62.54 crore of revenue earned through disposal of scrap.  
1.50 The Special Campaign 2.0 was implemented in Central Governm ent from October 2 -
October 31, 2022 with the objective of institutionalizing swachhata and minimizing pendency 
in government. Under the Special Campaign 2.0, 5.6 lac public grievances were redressed, 
cleanliness campaign was carried out in 1.01 lac office spaces, 37.50 lac files were weeded 
out, 89.5 lakh square feet of space was freed, and scrap disposal earned Rs. 370.1 crores. The 
special campaign 2.0 brought in a number of success stories in digitization, efficient 
management of office spaces, enhanceme nt of office premises, environment friendly 
practices, inclusivity, protocols and mechanisms being put in place and waste disposal.  

 
 
 
 36 
1.51 Departments/ Ministries gave special attention to attached/ subordinate/ field offices 
including in the remotest parts  of India in the month long campaign. Special Campaign 2.0 
was 17 times larger than Special Campaign of 2021 in terms of cleanliness campaign sites.  
1.52 The Special Campaign 2.0 was perhaps the biggest Campaign of office reforms in 
terms of size and scal e. It has helped decluttering offices, better space management and 
cleaner work environment in addition to effective management of records.  In order to 
maintain thrust of the campaign throughout the year and institutionalizing swachhata and 
decision-making reforms, the portal ( https://www.pgportal.gov.in/SCDPM/) and institution of 
nodal officers in each Ministry has been continued.  Ministries are uploading information on 
this portal every month and DARPG br ings out monthly publication on Secretariat Reforms 
based on the data uploaded by the Ministries.  Report of the month of April 2023 is enclosed. 
1.53 The Special campaign has now become a permanent activity and during October, 
2023, Special campaign 3.0 i s proposed to be undertaken with further enlargement of scope.  
This year the campaign is proposed to cover Ministries/ Departments, attached/ subordinate/ 
field offices, PSUs in the Central Government.  A meeting with Secretaries of Administrative 
Reforms of all States/ UTs was also held on 31st May, 2023 wherein they also showed 
willingness to participate in the month long Special Campaign during the month of October, 
2023.   Therefore, the Special campaign 3.0 is expected to be a much larger campaign 
covering all Offices of Government of India as well as the State/ UT Governments.    
1.54 Further,  with a view to encourage and develop a healthy competition  amongst all 
Ministries/ Departments for various activities under the Special campaign, a category i s 
proposed to be introduced in this year‘s prime Minister‘s Award for performance of 
Ministries/ Departments under the Special campaign, for which details are being worked out. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.55 The Committee recommends the Department to enco urage and aid the States also to 
carry out such campaigns for cleaning of State Government offices and attached/subordinate 
officers under the State Government, in a time-bound manner. (3.26) 
Action Taken  
1.56 A meeting with Secretaries of Administrative Reforms of all States/ UTs was held on 
31st May, 2023 to discuss recommendations of 127th Report of Parliamentary Standing 

 
 
 
 37 
Committee for replication/ dissemination of best practices of Special Campaign for 
institutionalizing Swachhata and reducing pendency and other initiatives of Secretariat 
reforms of the Government.  All States/ UTs expressed their willingness to participate in 
Special Campaign on Reducing pendency and institutionalizing Swachhata.  It was dec ided 
that DARPG will help the States to structure the Campaign and develop online system of 
coordination and monitoring of the Campaign.   As the Campaign of such a scale requires 
massive outreach and mobilization, DARPG also agreed to support the States i n developing 
Communication strategy for the Special Campaign in 2023.  
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR GOOD GOVERNANCE (NCGG) 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.57 The Committee appreciates the  Capacity Building Programme  conducted by NCGG 
in collaboration with different countries and recommends signing MoU with  more and more 
countries as the success of these programmes enhance the image not only of the institution 
but also of the country and plays a vital role to strengthen the bilateral relations. (3.31) 
Action Taken  
1.58 India has created a niche for itself in providing citizen -centric governance,  
progressive public policies, faster socio -economic development, high economic growth and  
attainment of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with speed and scale. This has 
improved the quality of life of citizens and world is talked about. Over the years, NCGG has 
been building its own capacity in these areas and has been able to create a name for itself on 
whom Ministry of External Affairs depends on developing and conducting need -based high 
quality capacity building programmes for the civil servants of developing countries and also 
giving advice to these governments. This brings a good name for the country and appreciated 
by the civil servants and government of various developing countries. 
1.59 NCGG designs and conducts comprehensive capacity building programmes for the 
civil servants of developing countries with the support of the Ministry of External Affairs. In 
2023-24, Ministry of External Affairs has substantially enhanced these programmes and 
approved45 capacity building programmes to impart training to 1,810 civil servants of 
Maldives, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Cambodia, Gambia, SriLanka, Mauritius, and other 
countries of Africa, LatinAmerica, etc. 

 
 
 
 38 
1.60 The modules for such programmes are developed in close collaboration with the 
concerned countries and Indian missions therein to meet their developmental needs. NCGG is 
in constant touch with the MEA for inclusion of more developing countries under the 
programme.The MEA has agreed in principle to include more countries in future and 
accordingly NCGG has planned to enhance and expand its own capacity in terms of human 
resources and domain expertise, and infrastructure facilities to include more developing 
countries in future programmes. 
Recommendation/Observation 
1.61 The Committee aspires to see NCGG as a 'world class institute' in the field of  good 
governance. For that NCGG has developed a strategy which includes having its  own campus 
and office space, suitable infrastructure, and additional human resources to carryout 
diversified activities. The Committee hopes that NCGG will  implement such strategies and 
act as a premier thinktank of the Government of India. (3.32) 
Action Taken  
1.62 NCGG being an apex level institution is visited by high level dignitaries viz. High 
Commissioners/ Ambassadors and senior diplomats of various countries, eminent people,  
senior civil servants, domain experts, academicians, heads of various institutions of India and 
abroad, etc. As recommended by the Committee, NCGG has to have decent facilities to  
engage with such high ranking and eminent people and convey the right image of the country 
and of the institution. 
1.63 As suggested by the Committee that NCGG should also have its own independent 
campus to do its mandated work more effectively and efficiently. The matter was discussed 
with the DARPG and Ministry of Finance. During the discussion, it was fully supported and 
indicated that once land and its cost, building, and infrastructure is firmed up, the proposal for 
capital cost will be considered in a holistic manner. In the meantime, NCGG can take office

in 2023-24totaketheofficespace on rent and develop commensurate facilities. 
1.64 In short-term, NCGG is focusing on improving its existing facilities at Mussoorie as

adequate steps to utilize the funds timely, completely and efficiently in future.

1.68 The chart clearly depicts the allocated amount and utilization pattern for such a very 
vital scheme of the Department. During 2021 -22 the BE allocation was Rs. 5 crores for the 
scheme, however, it got reduced to Rs. 3.31 crores at RE stage and at the end of the year only 
Rs.3.06 crores could be spent. The allocation for the BE 2022 -23 was Rs. 3.57 crores, which

of grievances (i.e., < 500).
